channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: Environmental agency warns of economic tree loss and greenhouse gas emissions from cooking fuel.

item.title: Sierra Leone vice presidents fail to reach presidency
item.description: No vice president has ever been elected president in Sierra Leone since independence.

item.title: Female artisanal miners report sexual violence in Kono district
item.description: Women working in abandoned diamond and gold pits in Jaiama Nimikor describe a pattern of rape and harassment while seeking income.

item.title: Tunisia and Libya seek joint roadmap to boost cooperation
item.description: Tunis hosted preparatory talks for the 23rd High Joint Commission session, which is due to be held in Tripoli.

item.title: Nachipanti victim speaks 17 years after family killings
item.description: Margaret Twalibu still suffers health issues from a 2009 attack that killed her sister and nephew.

item.title: UN adds FRN to DR Congo sanctions list
item.description: The UN Security Council's sanctions committee added the Front for the Nation's Refoundation as another name for the Alliance Fleuve Congo.

item.title: Namibia faces water supply strain
item.description: Central coast uses double its aquifer capacity, relying on desalination.

item.title: Polisario Front calls for general mobilisation as UN mission prepares to leave
item.description: The independence movement tells all Sahrawis to be ready to defend their land after the Security Council ends the Minurso mandate.

item.title: Amnesty: South Sudan failed to protect Abiemnom residents
item.description: Over 200 killed in March massacre despite prior warnings to government and UNMISS.

item.title: Tunisia forecasts strong winds, dust in the south and rough northern seas
item.description: Maximum temperatures of 27 to 32 degrees Celsius are expected on Thursday, November 12, 2026, with weak rain in the far north overnight.

item.title: Fake officer demands ID from real police
item.description: A 27-year-old man faces charges for impersonating an officer and threatening to arrest police.

item.title: Meatco suspends slaughter operations amid FMD crisis
item.description: Namibian beef exporter Meatco faces severe financial pressure and potential job cuts due to the suspension of international exports.

item.title: Chakwera given 7 days on MCP convention
item.description: Petitioners demand emergency convention, suspension of restructuring, and withdrawal of election fees.

item.title: Kenya seeks EU election observers for 2027 polls
item.description: President Ruto also requested European support to remove Kenya from money laundering watchlists.

item.title: Storms in Algeria injure two people and bring down a wall and four trees
item.description: Civil protection services recorded the damage in several wilayas on Thursday morning as strong winds swept through the country.

item.title: Sierra Leone seeks first AFCON qualifier points against DR Congo
item.description: The Leone Stars, still without a point in Group E, face DR Congo in Kinshasa in their third 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Thursday, November 12.

item.title: Three judicial experts sworn in at Bangui Court of Appeal
item.description: Jean Louis Hubert Benimet, Véronique Vondo, and Akpekabou Maleombho Djetou Madina will now provide technical advice to magistrates.

item.title: Liberian judges warn of court corruption
item.description: Circuit judges across Liberia used their court term openings to highlight systemic issues.

item.title: Russian embassy displays silk scarves in Conakry
item.description: An exhibition of Nina Routchkina's scarf designs opened at Guinea's National Museum on November 10, 2026.

item.title: Simba Queens and JKT win Women's Premier League matches
item.description: Simba Queens beat Mashujaa 2-0 while JKT edged Yanga Princess 1-0, and Bunda Queens' coach has called for better officiating.

item.title: Ghana urges bankable green projects at COP31
item.description: Minister Seidu Issifu called for concrete outcomes from China-Africa climate commitments at the Antalya conference.

item.title: Cameroon imports rise 22.8% in first quarter
item.description: Goods imports climbed 25.8% as the trade gap widened, according to the National Institute of Statistics.

item.title: Liberia's agriculture minister says US$13.1 million budget falls far short
item.description: Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah says the proposed FY2027 allocation is US$55.9 million below the ministry's US$69 million request.

item.title: Tanzania Post to judge regional managers on results
item.description: Regional managers and headquarters leaders will be assessed on business growth, resource use and service quality, with action for those who fall short.

item.title: Malawi presents automatic fuel pricing model at Windhoek regional meeting
item.description: Officials say the mechanism, adopted in 2012, has helped government save public money and free fiscal space for other priorities.

item.title: Niger journalists attend China information seminar
item.description: 20 Nigerien officials and journalists are in Beijing for a three-week seminar on Chinese governance and media cooperation.

item.title: Eswatini businesses flout laws
item.description: Nearly seven in 10 inspected firms failed to meet legal or regulatory standards.

item.title: Liberia wins African backing ahead of UN Security Council presidency
item.description: Ambassadors from 17 countries pledged regional support as Liberia readies to chair the 15-member Council in December 2026.

item.title: TanTrade boosts local production for export
item.description: Tanzania Trade Development Authority aims to increase value addition and market access for domestic products.

item.title: Guinea media regulator suspends journalist
item.description: The High Authority of Communication banned a journalist's Facebook page and revoked his press card.

item.title: Swimmer Matt Sates reportedly seeks Australian citizenship
item.description: The two-time South African Olympian could compete for Australia at the 2028 Los Angeles Games, according to a broadcaster's report.

item.title: Port-Louis road closure sparks traffic complaints
item.description: Emergency repairs on Rue Mgr Leen, closed since November 10, continue until December 21.

item.title: Botswana's President says fathers must care for children named by mothers
item.description: President Duma Boko says a man named as father is presumed to be the father until a DNA test proves otherwise.

item.title: Togo launches first cybersecurity event
item.description: The Togo Cyber Arena will gather public officials, companies, and experts on November 19-20 in Lomé.

item.title: Dolphin targets fibre blind spots in Zim broadband
item.description: The telecommunications group plans fixed wireless internet services for underserved areas.

item.title: Maraga accuses Ruto of hypocrisy over Ebola quarantine U-turn
item.description: Kenya begins a 42-day countdown to Ebola-free status after discharging its last patient and releasing final contacts from monitoring.

item.title: Nimba University suspends student leaders over protest
item.description: Two campus political group chairmen suspended for one to two semesters after disrupting senator's visit.

item.title: Nsekera brings sport to all Burundi communes
item.description: Lydia Nsekera has revitalized sports federations, bringing them out of obscurity and expanding access nationwide.

item.title: Mauritius central bank raises key rate to 5%
item.description: The Bank of Mauritius increased its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to combat rising inflation.

item.title: Institut Pasteur Dakar advances African health sovereignty
item.description: The institute is developing rapid diagnostics and resuming vaccine production to combat epidemics.

item.title: Liberia drug agency heads test negative for drugs
item.description: Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency director general and deputies passed drug tests before Senate confirmation hearings.

item.title: Siguiri ex-administrators return to prison as corruption trial is adjourned
item.description: Trial of 22 former territorial administrators and 202 gold panners resumes on November 16, 2026, after a lengthy day of confrontations.

item.title: SSPDF deploys troops for disarmament in Wau
item.description: South Sudan's army sent soldiers to Wau County to collect illegal firearms.

item.title: Nine civilians killed in Blue Nile drone strike
item.description: Displaced families fleeing fighting in Bani Shako village were targeted on Tuesday.

item.title: Senegal beach handball teams reach JOJ finals
item.description: Senegal's athletes are competing for 15 titles on the penultimate day of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games.

item.title: Airtel Tchad and ARCEP inspect network sites in N'Djamena
item.description: The operator's director general and the telecoms regulator's director general toured four sites after a formal notice of default.

item.title: 14,000 returnees receive aid in North Darfur
item.description: Displaced people return to 24 villages in Dar Al-Salam locality after fleeing attacks.

item.title: Young Zebras miss Ratshukudu for U-23 Cup qualifier
item.description: Botswana's Under-23 team faces Guinea without their top scorer, Losika Ratshukudu, who joins the senior squad.

item.title: Sifuna's Linda Mwananchi faces court challenge before Friday's delegates conference
item.description: A petitioner asks the Political Parties Disputes Tribunal to suspend the November 13 meeting that would formalise the party's transition from The Equitable Party.

item.title: FAM revives FA Cup with knockout format
item.description: The Football Association of Malawi will launch a new national cup competition involving teams from all levels of Malawian football.

item.title: Namibia's FMD-free suspension halts N$5.5 billion beef exports
item.description: Namibia's FMD-free status was suspended after a September 2026 biosecurity breach in //Kharas, stopping beef exports worth N$5.5 billion a year.

item.title: Mozambique police arrest sixth suspect in bishop's murder
item.description: A former soldier expelled for crimes is accused of carrying out the killing of Bishop Osório Citora Afonso.

item.title: Madagascar president targets 70% electricity access by 2030
item.description: President aims for ambitious goal while capital faces repeated, lengthy power cuts.

item.title: Logone Occidental launches training for 200 volunteer agents
item.description: The 200 recruits, drawn from education, health, environment and agriculture, will take part in a programme run with the national volunteering agency.

item.title: Naira slides against dollar as Thursday trading opens
item.description: Official and street rates diverge by roughly ₦68 to ₦80 per dollar as the currency faces pressure from importers and portfolio outflows.

item.title: Zesco targets 11,630MW by 2030
item.description: The state utility aims to exceed the government's 10,000MW goal by 1,630MW, a year ahead of schedule.

item.title: Chad's president holds security talks in Abéché
item.description: Mahamat Idriss Déby Itno met administrative, military and religious leaders in the Ouaddaï provincial capital on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

item.title: Samia demands fair carbon returns at COP31
item.description: Tanzania's president urged leaders in Antalya, Türkiye, to turn climate promises into investments for development.

item.title: Gambo hospital lacks basic facilities
item.description: A 1978 building in southeastern Central African Republic operates without an operating room or adequate medical supplies.

item.title: Zambia's proposed K22.7 billion farm budget wins praise from Kasama group
item.description: Impanga Emayo Business Hub says the 2027 National Budget proposal backs a sector the Grow Zambia Agenda treats as a key economic pillar.

item.title: MTN Uganda funds 25 community projects with Sh500 million
item.description: The telecommunications company's foundation will support initiatives in health, education, and environment.

item.title: Zambian mother seeks word on son detained in Mozambique
item.description: Grace Nampokolwe Banda has had no contact with her son Emmanuel, known as Jay Jay, since he was taken in Mozambique on October 14.

item.title: Ebola and insecurity worsen food crisis in eastern DRC
item.description: A UN food agency report shows the combined health and security crises have severely impacted agriculture and livelihoods.

item.title: Jauslin Laura finishes fifth in youth Olympic 200m
item.description: The Makis Ladies were the only Malagasy team to win a medal as the country's athletics programme at the Youth Olympic Games closed.

item.title: Doumbouya invites investors to Simandou 2040
item.description: Guinea's president promises a transformed nation and stable investment rules by 2040.

item.title: Libyan mountain municipalities give Dbeibah one week deadline
item.description: Local leaders demand funding for stalled development projects and reject recent cabinet financial allocations.

item.title: Walvis Bay handles N$13.2 billion in September trade
item.description: Namibia's trade deficit widened to N$4.7 billion as imports outpaced exports, with the port handling the bulk of goods by value.

item.title: Niger frees journalist Serge Mathurin Adou after two years in prison
item.description: Adou, a Nigerien-Ivorian journalist, was released on Wednesday, November 11, 2026, after being convicted of endangering state security.

item.title: Ghana businesses face 120% collateral barrier for loans
item.description: The Association of Ghana Industries says high loan security demands prevent firms accessing credit despite falling interest rates.

item.title: Two Comoros murder convicts die within a week
item.description: Fahami Moustoifa, sentenced to death, died on November 11, a week after Athoumane Abdourahmane.

item.title: Seven artists turn Antananarivo airport into showcase of Malagasy culture
item.description: Ravinala Airports has unveiled the works of seven winners from the second Art’ÉROPORT contest, chosen from nearly 50 applicants.

item.title: Four pupils die in suspected poisoning
item.description: Ta-Alim Primary School in Kisasi has been closed as police investigate the deaths of four young girls.

item.title: Uganda court hears Shs60bn bank fraud trial
item.description: Nine finance officials face charges over alleged diversion of $14 million to foreign firms.

item.title: Police target AI fake news farms before 2027 polls
item.description: Nigeria's police are deploying cyber-intelligence to find phone farms used to spread AI-generated disinformation.

item.title: Drought kills 99 cattle in Lavumisa, Eswatini
item.description: Farmers in Maplotini say the death toll has almost doubled since the previous week as water sources run dry.

item.title: Two old friends share grogue at local bar
item.description: Txiku Iaia and Ntoni Txéka, friends for over 50 years, met at their usual bar for drinks.

item.title: Eswatini youth delegate highlights child hunger
item.description: A 15-year-old delegate described schoolchildren fighting over food at a school visit.

item.title: Gowon memoirs praise Awolowo's economic leadership
item.description: General Yakubu Gowon's book highlights Chief Obafemi Awolowo's financial management during the civil war.

item.title: Senegal: 24 irregular migrants intercepted in Gambia
item.description: Gambian immigration services stopped 104 people, including 24 Senegalese nationals, in Mayamba and Batokunku.

item.title: Mauritania president meets Congolese counterpart
item.description: Mohamed Ould Cheikh Ghazouani met Denis Sassou Nguesso at the Antalya Leaders Summit.

item.title: Bouna mosque restored after two weeks of work
item.description: Artisans from several countries worked to save the mud-brick structure from time and climate change.

item.title: Rwanda pitches green industry investment at COP31 in Antalya
item.description: Prime Minister Dr Justin Nsengiyumva told the Antalya summit that green industrialisation can cut emissions while lifting growth and jobs.

item.title: Lesotho cuts diamond mine royalties to 6%
item.description: Government reduces payments for Letšeng mine due to global price drops and fuel costs.

item.title: Naledi Funeral Planners founder regains control
item.description: High Court judgment ends a 10-month power struggle threatening the funeral services provider.

item.title: Maseru memorial urges remembrance of mother and daughter's lives
item.description: Principal Secretary Thabang Lekhela asked the public to remember Hlompho and Liteboho Matsoso for their contributions, not their deaths.

item.title: Ha Belo factories near operational after power project completion
item.description: Unfinished industrial buildings in Botha-Bothe could soon create jobs as electrification nears completion.

item.title: Lesotho rugby president to serve as secretary-general of new regional body
item.description: Fetang Selialia, head of the Federation of Lesotho Rugby, has been appointed secretary-general of COSARU, a newly endorsed Southern African body.

item.title: AES ministers review second-year roadmap in Ouagadougou
item.description: Ministers from Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger are reviewing progress on the confederation's roadmap at a two-day session that ends with a synthesis note.

item.title: Lamin J. Darboe files nomination for Gambia presidential election
item.description: Team Gambia aspirant pledges rule of law and transparency if elected president on December 5.

item.title: Ghana urged to renegotiate low carbon credit prices
item.description: Minority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh says the proposed US$5 to US$25 per tonne range undersells Ghana's environmental resources.

item.title: Teenager charged with murder over Ghanaian boy's death in New York
item.description: A 17-year-old suspect faces murder charges for the fatal shooting of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong in the Bronx.

item.title: Ghana's Nana Dr. Antwi-Boasiako Amoah presses COP31 on climate finance
item.description: As chair of the African Group of Negotiators, Ghana's envoy says developed countries have no excuse to renege on their climate finance commitments.

item.title: Angola marks 51 years of independence at Cairo reception
item.description: Angola's ambassador to Egypt credits both presidents with strengthening ties, citing the Angola-Egypt Bilateral Commission as proof of the commitment.

item.title: Benin forestry agency publishes list of 135 eligible exam candidates
item.description: Candidates who passed the written tests for 135 posts in the Directorate-General of Water, Forests and Hunting now face medical checks next week.

item.title: Niamey traders close Grand Marché shops over Socogem rent rise
item.description: Some shopkeepers at Niamey's Grand Marché stayed shut in recent days to protest a sharp rise in shop rents set by Socogem.

item.title: Casablanca power cuts hit several districts
item.description: The SRM Casablanca-Settat cited a national grid incident for the widespread power outage affecting the city.

item.title: Tunisia chairs Arab health council meeting
item.description: Health Minister Mustapha Ferjani proposed an Arab network for medical simulation centers.

item.title: Storm knocks out power across Casablanca and nearby areas
item.description: A fault in the national transmission network left several Casablanca districts and Nouaceur province without electricity on Wednesday afternoon.

item.title: Lilongwe council buys three electric vehicles to beat fuel shortages
item.description: The city council has spent K615 million on three electric cars so officers can keep collecting revenue during fuel shortages.

item.title: South Sudan makes Friday a public holiday for Lagu's state funeral
item.description: Civil servants and staff of international organisations get the day off, and the burial begins with a 6 a.m. requiem at All Saints Cathedral in Juba.
